title: Organisms and Populations

standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations
standard_text: Population interactions – mutualism, competition, predation, parasitism; population attributes – growth, birth rate and death rate, age distribution.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 11 Organisms and Populations: population density, birth and death rates, growth models, age pyramids, adaptations and population interactions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Exponential growth is J-shaped; logistic growth is S-shaped.
body_html:
How to think about it

A population has attributes such as density, birth rate (natality), death rate (mortality), sex ratio and age distribution. Its size changes as Nt+1 = Nt + (B + I) − (D + E). With unlimited resources growth is exponential (dN/dt = rN, a J curve); with limited resources it is logistic (an S curve) and levels off at the carrying capacity K.

Species interact by mutualism (+/+), competition (−/−), predation and parasitism (+/−), commensalism (+/0) and amensalism (−/0). Organisms cope with unfavourable conditions by migration, hibernation, aestivation or diapause.

Example

N = 1000, B = 80, D = 50, I = 10, E = 20?

1000 + 90 − 70

Answer: 1020

Example

Orchid on mango branch?

+/0

Answer: commensalism

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting immigration and emigration.
  • Calling a lichen parasitism.
  • Saying logistic growth is J-shaped.
